title: Orion Commerce — Q2 Executive Engagement Briefing (Renewal-focused)

body:
Purpose: prep doc for a 45-minute executive QBR with Orion Commerce (e‑commerce platform, ~220M monthly impressions). Main objective is to secure a 12–18 month renewal for Redwood Dedicated and to expand Redwood Optimize pilot across two additional product lines. Secondary objective: align on SLO/SLAs and a phased rollout for vector search migration on private deployment.

Audience: Orion execs (VP Product - Sangeeta Rao, Head of Infrastructure - Marco Diaz, Director of Data Science - Alan Park), CSM + AE, Solutions Eng. Tone: concise, business-outcome oriented; avoid deep infra detail unless asked.

Slide-by-slide scripted narrative and tailored talking points: 

1) Opening + Objectives (5 min)
- CSM: "Thanks for the time. Today we'll surface the top-line outcomes Redwood has delivered, the small but high-impact operational gaps we see, and a concrete renewal proposal that reduces your unit cost while preserving query latency. Goal is to leave with agreement on a pilot expansion and a renewal term."
- Key ask on slide: "Approve pilot expansion to two more product lines (Cart Personalization, Post-purchase Recommendations). Confirm renewal cadence preference: annual vs 18-month with growth credits."

2) Current Health Snapshot: Business KPIs & Redwood ROI
- Talking points: "Since onboarding (Nov '25) Orion has used Redwood for recommendation generation and product copy augmentation. Measured outcomes: +4.2% add-to-cart rate on personalized recommendations, 12% faster time-to-publish for marketing copy pipelines, and estimated monthly cost reduction of 18% after quantization/Smart-batching. These map to ~$34k monthly savings vs baseline for peak traffic weeks."
- Visual: waterfall showing baseline cost, optimizations applied, and net savings.

3) Technical Signals: Latency, Errors, Cost per 1k Tokens
- Data we will show: P95 latency by route (recommendations: 165ms -> target 130ms), error rate (0.12% over 30d), cache hit-rate (prefix cache 48%), cost per 1k tokens (after batching: $2.87 equivalent).
- Tailored script: "Latency for recommendations is trending down with our suggested kernel selection; we propose a staged config change next week during low-traffic window to validate improvements. Error spike on 2/03 traced to model alignment mismatch — mitigated by routing fallback to a smaller variant."

4) Adoption Map: Teams, Routes, Models
- Table summary (read aloud): "3 product teams actively calling the API (Recommendations, Merchandising, Email Personalization). 7 production routes; top 3 consume 84% of token volume. Current model mix: open-llama-70b-quant for recommendations (batch-optimized), small turbo-variants for copy."
- Conversation starter: "Which internal roadmap items would benefit most from expanded Redwood Optimize recommendations?"

5) Case Highlight: Product Recommendations Flow
- Narrative: "Walk through a concrete customer example: Black Friday flow showed 18% increase in CVR on seeded cohorts when using session-aware prefix caching. Our technical change: KV caching per session + dynamic batching cut tail latency by 22% during peak."
- CSM talking point: "This is repeatable – we can template the same pattern for Cart Personalization pilot in 3 weeks."

6) Risks & Mitigations (renewal focus)
- Identified risks: (a) Cost creep if traffic spikes unpredictably, (b) Integration stretch for vector search migration, (c) Exec-level attention to vendor consolidation.
- Mitigations to propose: (a) Guardrails: token caps + auto-burst thresholds; (b) Dedicated SRE days and a migration runbook for vector indexing; (c) Executive sponsor cadence + monthly topline scorecard.
- Quick win to reduce perceived risk: 6-week cost-guardrail pilot that pauses non-critical routes if spend delta >15% week-over-week.

7) Proposed Roadmap + Quick Wins
- 0–6 weeks: Pilot expansion to Cart Personalization; implement cost-guardrail; autotune batching thresholds.
- 6–12 weeks: Private cluster pre-provision for vector search and run migration dry-run; deploy Optimize suggestions for model quantization across two model families.
- 3–6 months: Evaluate Dedicated autoscaling policy tweaks and agree renewal pricing tied to committed throughput.

8) Commercial Ask & Renewal Options
- Option A (preferred): 12-month renewal with 10% committed discount and 2 expansion credits (apply to pilot expansion). Includes 48h P1 SLA and 30 days extended observability retention for product routes.
- Option B: 18-month renewal with 15% discount, but vendor lock-in features require a 60-day exit notice. Comes with prioritized SRE allocation for vector migration.
- Walk the leadership through the math on slide: how preserving current config but adding Optimize saves ~12–18% on monthly spend under Option A.

9) Success Plan & SLAs for Next Contract
- Proposed KPIs to put into renewal SLOs: P95 recommendations latency <= 150ms, error rate <= 0.25%, prefix cache hit-rate >= 50%, measurable +3% CVR lift on piloted flows within 90 days of rollout.
- Operational commitments: monthly scorecard, quarterly executive touchpoint, playbook for incident postmortem within 72h.

10) Appendix: Data Definitions and Support Runbook
- Include definitions of: token accounting (how we count embeddings vs generation tokens), cost normalization, model variant compatibility matrix, and step-by-step contact tree for P0/P1 incidents.

Negotiation notes for AE + CSM (scripted):
- When asked about pricing flexibility: "We can prioritize credits for pilot expansion if the team signs to a 12-month commitment today. That buys you runway to prove the two new product lines and lock in the unit economics we presented."
- If execs push for lower discount: focus on operational risk reduction (SRE days, SLA terms) rather than deeper percent off.

Stakeholder map (recommended attendees for final renewal call):
- Orion: VP Product (Sangeeta Rao) - signs for product outcomes; Head of Infrastructure (Marco Diaz) - signs for capacity and network; Head of Procurement (TBD) - commercial terms; Director of Data Science (Alan Park) - technical validity.
- Redwood: AE (Liam Chen), CSM (Ethan Cole), Solutions Eng (Marisol Vega), SRE lead (Priya Natarajan).

Risks flagged to internal Redwood stakeholders: 
- Solutions Eng: need two dedicated 2-day SRE blocks in next 6 weeks for migration prep.
- Support: prepare an automated cost-alert channel; ensure on-call SRE has runbook for prefix cache invalidation.

Action items & timeline (owner / due date):
- Draft final renewal SOW and send to Orion Procurement (AE: Liam Chen) — due 2026-03-17.
- Schedule pilot kickoff for Cart Personalization (CSM: Ethan Cole + Solutions Eng) — target 2026-03-24.
- Implement cost-guardrail in staging and demo to Orion infra team (Infra: Priya Natarajan) — due 2026-03-12.
- Prep a short technical appendix describing vector migration steps for 1:1 with Director of DS (Marisol Vega) — due 2026-03-05.

Appendix (short):
- Glossary of metrics: P95 latency (ms), Cache hit-rate (% of tokens satisfied from prefix/KV cache), Token spend normalized to 1k tokens, Model variant cost multiplier (e.g., 70B = 1.0 baseline, 13B = 0.42).
- Support runbook excerpt: immediate remediation for high-tail latency: 1) throttle non-real-time routes, 2) force route fallback to lower-size variant, 3) open SE ticket and notify Orion infra Slack channel.

Notes to self (CSM): keep the opening focused on business outcomes, and defer detailed kernel/quantization discussion to the tech breakout. Reinforce value with the Black Friday CVR example and use the cost-guardrail as the primary lever for reducing renewal friction.

Optional attachments to include with the send: one-page ROI snapshot, 3-slide technical appendix, draft SOW template, pilot runbook checklist.

End of briefing draft.
